messages:
nina: Hey folks quick Q — I work 24 hrs/wk (part-time) and starting next month I want to max my 401(k) catch-up contributions (50+) and also use Roth deferrals. Does Redwood allow Roth + catch-up if I'm part-time? Also any rules around hardship withdrawals? cc @carlos

carlos (People Ops): Short: yes you can do Roth deferrals and catch-up contributions if eligible, but eligibility for catch-up depends only on age (50+) not full-time status. We apply payroll deferrals per paycheck; part-time just means smaller per-paycheck amounts to reach limits.

rachel (Benefits): A few practical bullets: 1) Roth elective deferrals are allowed alongside pre-tax. 2) Catch-up contributions for 50+ can be designated Roth catch-up if your plan permits Roth catch-ups — ours does. 3) Annual IRS limits apply (regular + catch-up). 4) Hardship withdrawals: our plan offers in-plan hardship distributions only if criteria in the SPD are met; they are limited and documentation is required.

sam (Payroll): Enrollment notes: - Set your deferral % in Workday; for Roth vs pre-tax you choose the split. - To hit annual max as a part-timer you may need a higher %; check projected per-paycheck math. - Payroll cutoff is the 5th 23:59 PT for next cycle. If you want help calculating %, DM me your salary and pay frequency and I can run numbers.

nina: Helpful thanks. For hardship, does taking one mean I can't make elective deferrals for a while? Any tax/reporting differences?

rachel (Benefits): Hardship distributions are taxable (pre-tax portion) and could be subject to penalty if under 59½ unless exception applies. Some hardship distributions prevent certain types of deferrals for a period depending on plan rules; ours requires a 6-month suspension of elective deferrals in a narrow set of cases — see SPD. We'll pull the exact clause if you want.

carlos (People Ops): If you plan to do Roth catch-up and want to front-load the year, consider the contribution limits and potential payroll limits per paycheck. Also if you have outside IRAs you can roll them in later; roll-ins don't change catch-up eligibility.

hr-bot: Reminder: Benefits enrollment window and 401k deferral change steps are here: https://hr.redwood.example/benefits-401k. Onboarding checklist updated for new hires and catch-up guidance doc attached.

nina: Great — please pull the SPD excerpt on hardship and I'll DM Sam my pay cadence for the math. Thanks everyone!
